next: SonoJot Punctuation v4 can be downloaded from Models and is what new installs get: it adds capitals for names, places and acronyms with any speech model and keeps v3's punctuation, written forms and filler removal, and at 181 MB it is a smaller download than v3 (303 MB).
If a punctuation model on your computer cannot be opened, SonoJot uses the previous installed one instead of basic punctuation rules.
Amounts like 'twelve hundred dollars' are written as $1,200 when the punctuation model marks them.
After 'p.m.' the next word no longer starts a new sentence, so 'two thirty p.m. on Tuesday' stays one sentence.

Dictation with SonoJot Parakeet, or with Qwen3-ASR on a graphics card or Mac, now listens in longer stretches (up to 30 s for Parakeet, 60 s for Qwen) and misses fewer words, while the text is still ready just as quickly after you press Stop.

A meeting's Clean copy now runs the same cleanup as dictation and applies the corrections SonoJot has learned from your dictations, passage by passage; passages you edited keep your words, and the transcript itself never changes.

With SonoJot Punctuation v4, cleanup capitalises names, places and acronyms the speech model wrote in lower case, works the same with every speech model, and lowers a capital only when it is very sure; vocabulary words are never changed.
A capital letter A used as a label, as in 'option A', keeps its capital.

Adding a computer to sync no longer needs six digits or an Approve button: after the email sign-in, it gets the key on its own from any of your other computers that has SonoJot open, and keeps waiting until one does.
Your other computers show an alert when a computer joins sync, with OK and Not me; Not me removes that computer and changes the key.
The recovery code stays tucked away behind Use recovery code instead, and approved computers keep account management behind Account options.
Removing this computer signs it out without trying to show a new recovery code.
Missing meeting files require confirmation before mass deletion, and reappearing files cancel queued deletions.
Recently deleted restores missing audio and sidecars without overwriting an existing meeting.
Sync now reports meeting results and retries failed meetings without slowing the rest of the library.
Meeting edits and deletions made in older builds are preserved when returning to Nightly.
Large meeting libraries resume sync across rate limits, and a busy or damaged meeting no longer stalls the others or vocabulary sync.
Recently deleted lets you restore a meeting on this computer or remove its saved copy; unsynced audio requires confirmation before remote deletion.
Unreadable meeting layers and trash cleanup failures no longer hide the meeting library.
Dictations made with SonoJot Parakeet no longer capitalise a word in the middle of a sentence after a pause.
Highlighted choices, such as the selected fix in the doubtful-words card, now look like raised paper instead of plain white, and focus rings go round the whole control.

Meetings on speakers: Remove speaker echo (Sources and speakers) removes the other people's words that your microphone picked up, so they no longer appear twice as yours. It is on automatically with SonoJot Parakeet and off with Qwen until you turn it on; turn it off and transcribe again to get the unfiltered text.
Meetings and imported recordings transcribed with Parakeet on an NVIDIA graphics card no longer stop partway through long stretches of speech.
A meeting's Clean copy no longer capitalises a word in the middle of a sentence after a pause, as dictation already did not.

After a paste, SonoJot marks the few words it doubts right in the app you pasted into: hover to hear them, pick a fix, keep them, or hold the dictation key and say the word. Settings: Dictation, Doubtful words.
A test copy of SonoJot started with its own data folder no longer adds itself to coding tools.
Set up sync and Add this computer now open SonoJot email-code pages, with a clear recovery-code step for your first computer.
Removing a lost device changes the encryption key; your other trusted computers update automatically on their next sync, and SonoJot asks you to save the new recovery code.

Cleanup puts back the space before words like 'cause, 'til and 'em when the speech model joins them to the previous sentence, and Clean keeps leading apostrophes, opening quotes and brackets in place.
Switching update channels offers a clear download and restart action, or explains when no build is available for your computer.
Nightly releases now include signed and notarized builds for Apple Silicon Macs when the Mac build succeeds.
Builds without a configured staging server keep vocabulary sync disabled and explain why.
Meeting deletions received through sync require encrypted confirmation and keep the local files in trash for 30 days.
Large meeting transcripts sync in parts, and re-keying supports large meeting libraries without downloading their audio.
Interrupted meeting audio uploads can resume after expiry; unused uploads and old text layers are reclaimed safely.
Staging meeting storage defaults to 2 GB, with 100 GB reserved for designated test accounts and a daily upload limit.
Stable builds keep the existing local meeting format without creating sync layers.
Nightly and Sync Test builds can sync meeting transcripts, notes and edits through staging, with choices for edits made on two devices.
Meeting audio sync is optional and off by default, with a separate choice for each meeting and downloads when needed.
Meeting audio sync uses 64 kbps Opus and shows an estimate of storage per minute.
Account and sync shows meeting storage; the oldest meetings stop syncing only after a device confirms a complete local copy.
Mac sync sign-in explains keychain errors; the separate Sync Test app can save its test credentials without unlocking the login keychain.
Encrypted vocabulary sync is available in nightly and other prerelease builds; stable builds keep sync disabled.
Sync Test can sign into isolated staging test accounts and pause its connection from the command line.
The Updates screen and the update prompt are tidier: buttons line up, and a long download no longer pushes the side bar out of place.
After an update, SonoJot no longer says it closed unexpectedly. It shows what's new instead.
See changes shows what an update brings before you install it, and What's new in Settings > Updates shows the notes for your version.
Meetings and imported recordings miss fewer words, including quiet speech such as a stretch where you sit back from the microphone.

New speech model: SonoJot Parakeet, our own tuned version of Parakeet. It makes about a fifth fewer errors on dictation than Parakeet in our tests, at the same size and speed. It replaces Parakeet in the speech list. If you use Parakeet now, nothing changes until you choose the new one.

New English setups now start on SonoJot Parakeet for dictation and meetings on every computer, including NVIDIA PCs and Macs. It ties Qwen3-ASR on meetings in our tests and is faster and smaller. Qwen3-ASR stays one tap away in Speech as the multilingual choice, other languages keep Qwen, and your saved choices do not change.
On a Mac, the Speech screen now shows word errors measured in the Mac app for SonoJot Parakeet and Qwen3-ASR, and the chart marks SonoJot Parakeet as recommended.

The Speech page is calmer: each model is one simple card with a short line, and the details sit behind a small i button. Compare models opens one chart of every model this computer can run, for everyday speech, accented English or talks, with a table of the same numbers. In Cleanup, Punctuation and the optional Proofreader now have their own rows, and the details for other settings moved behind i buttons.
Sync sign-in codes and security emails now come from SonoJot itself, and when a computer joins your sync you get an email straight away that names it (Mac, Windows PC or Linux computer).
SonoJot Parakeet has an update that makes fewer mistakes in meetings, at the same size and speed. If you already have it, SonoJot offers the update with one click and keeps your choices.

Models now update in place: a newer version of a model you have replaces the old one without choosing it again. The punctuation model updates by itself; larger speech models ask first. The old version keeps working until the new one has downloaded, checked out and loaded, and its files are removed after.

Doubtful words on the Mac: the "to check" chip now appears at the text cursor (or beside the pointer when an app hides it) instead of the window corner, hides itself after a few seconds and when you start the next dictation, and the panel plays the doubtful stretch once, closes with the close button or K, and draws a missing word as a small marker.
Rename a speaker by selecting their name in a meeting transcript, then choose whether to change every passage with that name or only the one you selected.
A meeting's title has a pencil button for renaming it.

The meeting's options moved under an export button whose first choice exports rich text (.rtf) for Word, Pages or Google Docs; Export other formats has Markdown, plain text, rich text, web page, PDF and the recording.
The meeting header is shorter: the date, length and number of speakers. The audio source and the auto-named and missing-seconds tags are gone from the header and the meeting list.
The Export button on a meeting in the list saves rich text (.rtf) instead of Markdown.

With sync on, a small cloud beside a meeting shows whether it is synced, uploading or downloading; selecting a download moves that meeting to the front of the queue, and the meeting's sync choices are under Sync in the export menu.
With SonoJot Punctuation v4, Clean no longer drops symbols between words: a percent sign, emoji, accents and `backticks` stay as you said them, and text in backticks keeps its exact wording.

Compare models opens one chart of every model this computer can run, for everyday speech, accented English or talks, with a table of the same numbers. In Cleanup, Punctuation and the optional Proofreader now have their own rows, and the details for other settings moved behind i buttons.
Sync sign-in codes and security emails now come from SonoJot itself, and when a computer joins your sync you get an email straight away that names it (Mac, Windows PC or Linux computer).
SonoJot Parakeet has an update that makes fewer mistakes in meetings, at the same size and speed. If you already have it, SonoJot offers the update with one click and keeps your choices.

Models now update in place: a newer version of a model you have replaces the old one without choosing it again. The punctuation model updates by itself; larger speech models ask first. The old version keeps working until the new one has downloaded, checked out and loaded, and its files are removed after.

SonoJot Punctuation v4 can be downloaded from Models and is what new installs get: it adds capitals for names, places and acronyms with any speech model and keeps v3's punctuation, written forms and filler removal, and at 181 MB it is a smaller download than v3 (303 MB).
If a punctuation model on your computer cannot be opened, SonoJot uses the previous installed one instead of basic punctuation rules.
Amounts like 'twelve hundred dollars' are written as $1,200 when the punctuation model marks them.
After 'p.m.' the next word no longer starts a new sentence, so 'two thirty p.m. on Tuesday' stays one sentence.

Dictation with SonoJot Parakeet, or with Qwen3-ASR on a graphics card or Mac, now listens in longer stretches (up to 30 s for Parakeet, 60 s for Qwen) and misses fewer words, while the text is still ready just as quickly after you press Stop.

A meeting's Clean copy now runs the same cleanup as dictation and applies the corrections SonoJot has learned from your dictations, passage by passage; passages you edited keep your words, and the transcript itself never changes.

With SonoJot Punctuation v4, cleanup capitalises names, places and acronyms the speech model wrote in lower case, works the same with every speech model, and lowers a capital only when it is very sure; vocabulary words are never changed.
A capital letter A used as a label, as in 'option A', keeps its capital.

Your other computers show an alert when a computer joins sync, with OK and Not me; Not me removes that computer and changes the key.

A new look. SonoJot now has four places down the left side: Dictation, Meetings, Words and Settings. Each list has a status band on top that shows what is ready and opens the right setting when something needs attention.
Speech models are compared on one chart of measured speed and memory, with the recommended choices shown first.
Choose your update channel in Settings > Updates: Stable, or Nightly for early test builds. Switch back to Stable at any time.
Meetings: rename a speaker or move a single passage to another speaker, search titles, notes and transcripts, and pick a notes style that is written automatically after each transcription.
Words: a word on its own is now a hint that helps SonoJot spell it without forcing a replacement. "Heard as > written" rules still replace exactly.
Dictation: export any dictation as Markdown, and choose to keep nothing, text, or text and audio. Audio stays on your computer for 30 days.
Fixes: pasted API keys stay hidden, shortcuts and notes instructions are checked before saving, and an update now finishes even when the command-line tool is running.

New, experimental: proofread your dictations with an online model. Turn on "Proofread with an online model" in Dictation to fix misheard words, typos and false starts while keeping your wording. It uses your own OpenRouter account and is off unless you turn it on.
Shape by type is easier to find: it now has its own row in Dictation. A new option, "Use the app I'm in", lays out text to suit where you are typing.
Saved dictations now note which app they were meant for, on your computer only. The privacy notice and terms describe both changes.
